tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...', 'Apply it to...'), focuses on triggering conditions a user/agent would observe (error codes, hangs, service states) rather than internals, explicitly lists multiple trigger contexts including vague phrasing ('won't start' or 'hangs' without naming a service), and is a tight, dense paragraph without being bloated.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a Windows Server EC2 instance's patching is blocked by a Windows update service or runtime fault rather than component-store corruption. Use it when a patch run fails with 0x80070422 ... including when the user only says patching "won't start" or "hangs" without naming a service.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps straight into domain-specific facts (service names, error codes, exact fix commands) without explaining generic concepts the agent already knows. It is dense but every line is specific knowledge, not filler.
tests.evidence: wuauserv Disabled (0x80070422, StartType: Disabled): SSM can start a Stopped/Manual service but cannot start a Disabled one.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: The skill is appropriately prescriptive for fragile operations (exact commands for re-enabling services, GAC registration) while still explaining the WHY (GPO re-disable, SSU link) rather than being rigid without reason.
tests.evidence: Set-Service -StartupType Automatic first. And if a GPO disabled it, it will re-disable on refresh (~90 min) — the GPO is the real fix.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Each fault path specifies one clear fix/tool (e.g., gacutil /i, msiexec /unregister then /regserver) rather than listing multiple equal alternatives.
tests.evidence: Re-register AWSSDK.Core.dll into the GAC with gacutil /i (snapshot first).

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic and recovery procedure (classify fault → route → fix → verify) applicable to any instance with this fault class, not a one-off instance-specific declaration.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Classify the service/runtime fault before acting... Step 2: Route to the fault (load the matching reference)

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A dedicated Gotchas section lists concrete, non-obvious corrections specific to this domain (Disabled vs Stopped, GPO re-disable, AV exclusion, DataStore.edb caution).
tests.evidence: Disabled ≠ Stopped. SSM/patch baseline can start a Stopped/Manual service but not a Disabled one
